title: Core Security finite dynamic-import target registration

decision_scope.question: Should the source-owned finite Core Security facade map be represented as a source-derived allowed-target set in the existing dynamic-import registry, separately from the registry-wide dated owner review?

source_route.current_collector_notes: User/plugin supplied module name; call site is inventoried for review.

source_object_denominator.mapping: The facade's immutable _EXPORTS mapping is the source map; __all__ names match its keys.

complete_denominator_receipt.scope_limit: Static source map and module-file census; no production import, runtime find_spec, or import result was exercised.

proposed_target_set_ref.note: The exact 26 module names are retained in the cited proposal, not duplicated here.

canonical_collector.behavior: The scanner retains source-derived import, tuple, mapping, and MappingProxyType bindings, and resolves a PEP 562 export for a requested symbol. At the dynamic-call sink, _call_pattern currently uses a literal argument or its expression text; _allowed_targets_for_pattern derives targets for literal polisyos modules and known entry-point groups, not a complete finite value set flowing through module_name. The current canonical row therefore has an empty allowed_targets list.
canonical_collector.row_validation: validate_dynamic_imports recomputes the source inventory and compares row signatures and the complete expected/observed field sets and values. It also checks each registered allowed target with importlib.util.find_spec. A manually inserted 26-target row does not match the current canonical collector; a manually inserted empty row can represent the current collector output but fails to bind the known finite map and remains review-required under ADR-RSR-0141.
not_run: Runtime import of the Core Security facade or any target

date_and_issuer_checks.inventory_gate: validate_dynamic_imports treats review_owner, reviewed_at, and review_expires as external review fields: it requires nonempty strings but does not compare them to the renderer, authenticate an issuer, or check expiration.

closeout_gate.behavior: Requires review_owner, reviewed_at, review_expires and an issue/ADR reference; parses review_expires and reports expired when it is earlier than today's date; rejects a future reviewed_at. It does not authenticate that the configured review_owner issued the decision.
closeout_gate.current_effect: As of 2026-10-16, the configured 2026-08-04 expiry is past and the closeout check is red unless a legitimate registry-wide review decision is issued. This is a source-code trace, not a claim that the full closeout command was run.

current_header.interpretation: These are configured strings, not proof of a named issuer or a current review. No date, expiry, owner, or clock change is proposed.

existing_decision_contract.relevant_rule: The registry is source of truth for dynamic import patterns; canonical rows are fully compared; empty allowed_targets are still review-required; review_owner/reviewed_at/review_expires are external decisions and inventory reconciliation neither issues nor renews them.

engineering_recommendation.disposition: Reuse registry version 1 and the existing complete source-derived row comparison; compose the route with the ongoing generic B61 source-binding work. Do not add a Core Security special case or a hand-maintained target whitelist.
engineering_recommendation.same_class_bucket: P40 SAME_CLASS_DEEPER: dynamic-import source-value provenance at the sink. Fold this route into the generic source-binding mechanism already in progress. If it remains outside that mechanism, record a bounded residual for finite source-owned values passed to import_module and use the add/remove/opaque-map falsifier; do not patch another individual source instance.
engineering_recommendation.minimal_generic_behavior: Pass the scanner's proven argument binding into dynamic-call row construction. For a complete, exact, immutable finite mapping whose selected value is a module string or a statically proven module component, derive the sorted distinct module set for allowed_targets. Preserve an empty target set for opaque, mixed, mutated, unresolved, or partial provenance; fail collection closed when guarded importer provenance becomes ambiguous. Keep existing literal and entry-point handling unchanged.

canonical_footprint.role: Extend existing source-binding/scanner-to-sink collection and canonical rendering/validation; do not create a parallel registry or route-specific rule.

Mirror generic finite-map coverage, exact row recomputation, target addition/removal drift, opaque/mixed fail-closed behavior, and unaffected literal/entry-point controls. The test should remove the source-derived target binding while leaving registry declarations intact and observe a mismatch/refusal.
Regenerate the one canonical row from source only after the collector can reproduce its exact target set; the row should name the existing verifier and preserve global header review metadata.

schema_and_migration.registry_version: Remain at version 1; allowed_targets and full-row comparison already exist, so this is an improvement to source derivation rather than a schema change.
schema_and_migration.migration: After the generic collector is accepted, regenerate the registry to add one row with the 26 source-derived module targets. The existing target-resolution gate then checks those modules. No per-target rows, exception, waiver, or blanket module promotion is needed.
schema_and_migration.separate_release_or_api_change: None proposed. This inventory change does not establish runtime import success, security review, or broader public API guarantees.

g_choice.recommended_choice: Treat the source map as a finite, source-owned dynamic-import registration once the generic collector proves the exact 110-alias-to-26-module mapping; keep dated owner review as a separate registry-wide authority decision.

options.choice: Source-derived finite registration plus separate dated registry review
options.assessment: Recommended. Engineering can derive the finite map from source without an authority expansion. A named accountable issuer must separately review the global registry before its expired review metadata is renewed.

options.choice: Register this as an empty-target user/plugin slot
options.assessment: Not recommended. It matches current collector output but contradicts the statically finite source map and leaves all 26 module targets unbound; ADR-RSR-0141 says empty target lists remain review-required.

options.choice: Insert the 26 targets manually into dynamic.toml
options.assessment: Rejected. The production validator compares the complete row to collector output, so the hand-maintained row is not canonical and can drift from source.

options.choice: Change review dates, reviewer strings, expiry rules, or exception policy to obtain a green gate
options.assessment: Rejected. This would alter authority/time semantics without an issuer decision and would conflate source inventory with review approval.

minimum_named_issuer_input_if_G_requires.identity: Name the accountable person or authorized review body; the current string team-architecture is not authenticated by the validator and the path-derived owner is not an approval record.
minimum_named_issuer_input_if_G_requires.scope: Explicitly state that the review covers the complete dynamic-import registry (currently 250 rows, and 251 after the proposed route row if no other rows change), not only this Core Security facade.
minimum_named_issuer_input_if_G_requires.decision: Record accept/refuse, rationale, any conditions, and the pinned registry/source frame reviewed.
minimum_named_issuer_input_if_G_requires.time: The issuer supplies the actual reviewed_at and review_expires values; do not infer or shift dates. The existing closeout gate checks expiry and rejects future review dates.
minimum_named_issuer_input_if_G_requires.reference: Provide the actual issue/ADR or governed review record. Existing field presence alone does not prove issuer identity.

g_choice.authority_state: No G acceptance, named security reviewer, or fresh registry-wide review record is established by the inspected source and receipts.

prototype.result: 110/110 alias coverage; 26 module source objects; add/remove target controls detected; opaque or mixed values remain unallowlisted.
prototype.limit: AST-only prototype, no product imports, no runtime find_spec, and no production validator execution. It is not a production proof.

facade.observed_shape: Immutable _EXPORTS mapping; __all__ has the same 110 names; __getattr__ resolves the requested map entry, imports module_name, then gets the named attribute.

test_that_checks_closeout_date.assertion: The phase 6.5 closeout test requires review_expires >= today; no test output was run for this packet.

pattern_pass.P31: Fix the generic source-value binding class, not this facade alone.
pattern_pass.P35: Use the complete 110-alias, 26-module, 250-row denominators and their pinned receipts.
pattern_pass.P37_P38: The collector recomputes row structure but currently sees only expression text at this dynamic sink; the exact finite target property is unmeasured there. The separate closeout gate recomputes date expiry, while reviewer identity remains an unauthenticated string.
pattern_pass.P40: Same class, one level deeper; compose with B61's generic source binding and do not create a per-instance allowance.

application_status: Decision packet only. No source, test, dynamic.toml, expiry, owner, or exception-policy change is included or applied.
review_request: G review: decide whether to accept the source-owned finite target registration as an engineering inventory fact, and separately identify the accountable issuer/process for the overdue registry-wide review.
